item.title: Kashkari Says Fed Should Raise Rates Now to Bring Down Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said the US central bank should start to raise interest rates incrementally right now to curb inflation that remains too high.

item.title: Amazon’s Zoox to Levy Fares, in US First for Controls-Free Taxis
item.description: Amazon.com Inc.’s Zoox robotaxi division will start charging fares next week in Las Vegas, marking a first in the US for autonomous vehicles without driver controls.

item.title: Meta Apologizes to Indian Officials Over Removal of Modi’s Video
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. apologized to Indian officials for temporarily restricting a Facebook post of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking to assuage the government’s concerns in a key growth market.

item.title: Brazil’s CSN Seeks $2.9 Billion for Sales of Entire Cement Unit
item.description: Benjamin Steinbruch’s Cia. Siderúrgica Nacional is seeking at least 15 billion reais ($2.9 billion) for its cement business and expects to receive four bids as it moves to sell the entire unit, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Services Activity Continues to Expand on Resilient Demand
item.description: The US service sector expanded at a steady pace in July, bolstered by a pickup in new orders and business activity.

item.title: Vusion Explores Strategic Options, Including Possible Sale
item.description: Vusion is in the early stages of exploring strategic options, including a potential sale, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: SpaceX’s $101 Billion Unlock Heaps Pressure on Battered Shares
item.description: Investors hanging onto SpaceX shares after a plunge below their IPO price are bracing for the next potential hit, when $101 billion worth of stock becomes available for trading on Thursday.

item.title: Stray Piece of SpaceX Falcon 9 Rocket Slams Into the Moon
item.description: A leftover piece of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket likely slammed into the surface of the moon early Wednesday, about 18 months after being sent into orbit.

item.title: PayPal Puts Revenue Targets on Key Units as CEO Reviews Strategy
item.description: PayPal Holdings Inc.’s new chief executive officer, who’s stayed quiet publicly as potential suitors circle the firm, said he plans for the first time to break out results and assign revenue targets for its three main businesses to give investors a better sense of the units’ potential.

item.title: US Keeps Debt-Sale Guidance Steady, Deepening Bill Reliance
item.description: The US Treasury on Wednesday retained its previous guidance for future debt issuance, signaling no change in note and bond auction sizes well into 2027 even as federal borrowing needs climb.

item.title: Knot Backed by Dutch Government to Replace Lagarde at ECB
item.description: The Netherlands endorsed Klaas Knot to lead the European Central Bank, as the race to succeed Christine Lagarde nears a decisive phase.

item.title: US Companies Added 44,000 Jobs in July, ADP Data Show
item.description: US companies added fewer jobs in July than expected, suggesting some cooling in hiring momentum after a recent stretch of solid gains.

item.title: Africa’s Highest Yielder Tops Debt Returns as Investors Turn Bullish
item.description: Gabon has become a top performer in emerging sovereign bond markets, buoyed by expectations that an International Monetary Fund program will help it avert a debt restructuring.

item.title: ZIG/USD: Zimbabwe Won’t Rush US Dollar Phase-Out Until Inflation Stabilizes
item.description: Zimbabwe won’t rush to phase out the US dollar and make the ZiG its sole currency until it is confident that inflation is under control and the exchange rate is stable.

item.title: S&P 500 Poised for Another Record as AI Spending Narrative Holds
item.description: Futures climbed on Wednesday as the latest batch of earnings pointed to strong demand for, and spending on, artificial intelligence. SpaceX reported higher-than-expected AI-related outlays, which overshadowed results that broadly beat forecasts, while Nvidia Corp. rallied after Elon Musk touted his computing plans.

item.title: Trump Borrows From Democrats’ Playbook With Attack on High Gas Prices
item.description: President’s criticisms of Big Oil echo the strategy used by his predecessor.

item.title: Kenya Seeks $450 Million World Bank Funds to Offset Iran War Shock
item.description: Kenya is in talks for about $450 million of emergency financing from the World Bank to cushion the economy from the impact of the Iran war and potential weather shocks, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Google Loses Bid to Block UK Class Action Over Search Ads
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google must face a class action lawsuit over alleged abuse of its dominance after an antitrust tribunal allowed a claim on behalf of hundreds of thousands of British firms to go ahead.

item.title: Prudential, HSBC Shares Tumble on China Insurance Tax Report
item.description: Prudential Plc, HSBC Holdings Plc and Standard Chartered Plc shares dropped after a report that China is expanding its personal income tax to include any returns from insurance policies in Hong Kong.

item.title: Shopify Shares Soar as Revenue Outlook Beats Estimates
item.description: Shopify Inc. shares rose as much as 33.8% in premarket trading after its third-quarter revenue outlook beat expectations.

item.title: Carry Trade Is Powering On as Investors Sidestep Yen’s Gains
item.description: Emerging-market carry trades, some of this year’s most popular foreign-exchange bets, are showing resilience even after joint US-Japan currency intervention dented the appeal of this yen-funded strategy.

item.title: Norway Home Prices Surprise by Falling the Most Since Pandemic
item.description: Norway’s underlying home prices unexpectedly fell the most in more than six years, in what some analysts attributed to lower activity among buyers and sellers because of the football World Cup.

item.title: AI Chatbots Seen in Survey as More Trustworthy Than Politicians
item.description: Survey finds people view chatbots as providing more accurate, useful information than local leaders

item.title: Tech Euphoria Has Come Back in Just Four Days
item.description: Sentiment has turned around completely from last month.

item.title: El Niño Raises Risk of Weather Shocks Across Global Economies
item.description: The tropical Pacific climate pattern is no longer just a weather event — it has become a significant macroeconomic variable.

item.title: Rhine and Danube rivers and drought and industry
item.description: Droughts have left the Rhine and Danube rivers at historically low levels

item.title: Uber Gives In-Line Outlook, Says Brazil Rivals Hurt Trips Growth
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. issued a bookings outlook that just met analyst estimates and said fierce competition in the key Brazil market weighed on trips volume, compounding concerns from investors about the company’s ability to evolve in the robotaxi era.

item.title: Kazakhstan Eyes Return to Panda Bonds With $500 Million Deal
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to return to the yuan debt market this year as Central Asia’s largest oil producer seeks to tap cheaper financing from China.

item.title: Bezos, Arnault, Premji Pour Money Into AI Humanoid Robot Startups
item.description: Family offices are particularly well-positioned to make these wagers.

item.title: Katayama Cites Bessent’s Faith in Japan’s Improving Fiscal Path
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sees Japan’s fiscal condition improving, according to Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, who spoke after Bessent gave a series of interviews in the wake of Washington’s move to help Tokyo prop up the yen last week.
